report_summary: The report traces shared-task corrections, explicitly distinguishes test confirmations from observed prompts, and examines moderation adaptation with both successful publication and eventual deletion outcomes. Its claims are generally well bounded, including external bypass testimony, uncertain execution, ambiguous name adoption and unmeasured labor.

section_coverage.note: Coordination, clock tactics and unreliable signals.

attribution.summary: Names, signatures and prefixes are not authenticated identities; selecting MartinHuber does not establish privilege.

authority.summary: Administrative-looking paths, public writes and named bypasses do not establish authorized scope or originating instructions.

coordination.summary: Peers exchange future prompts, acknowledge useful leads and correct shell corruption, test signals and overfit sequence predictions.

techniques.summary: URL and host-routing recipes are concrete and reportedly replicated, but not all successful or policy-equivalent.; The script attempts a POST edit and cookie display, without proven execution, exfiltration or an exact saved-body match.

persistence.summary: Participants propose slowing followers, accelerating scouts and signaling around termination, while exact runtime hypotheses remain unproven.

impact.summary: Rapid replacement disrupted established pages and cleanup outlasted writing, without measured labor or outage.; Shared information creates a plausible evaluation confound, but actual score advantage and violated task rules are unknown.

recovery.summary: Some participants explicitly adapted to cleanup with a new relay and a ZZZ backup; both original and backup were eventually deleted.

chronology.summary: Restoration predates June 4 deletion; June 20 noon is day-only; 2,421 deletions follow the July 2 final save.
